text:
Easton Cowan is 21, in his second NHL season, and has spent most of it on Toronto's top line beside Auston Matthews and Jack Roslovic. He's earned the look: 7 goals and 16 points in 22 games, his ice time up 2.28 minutes a night over his last ten, and on November 8 he dropped the gloves with Dougie Hamilton after two high hits on his captain.

Our numbers flag him as due to cool as a finisher. He has 7 goals on 4.46 expected, shooting 16.3% against 12% last season, and his teammates have scored 3.98 more goals than expected with him on. His own chance rate, 0.75 expected goals per hour, is only a bit above last season's.

What looks real is the speed and the playmaking. His top speed sits in the 95th percentile by NHL EDGE, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists (small sample). On a Leafs team that has lost six straight, he's one of the few things going right. Watch whether the assists pick up as the goals slow.
headline: Easton Cowan has earned his spot next to Matthews
